_comment: IGT is not a table. Snow Peak calls it the LAYOUT SYSTEM (レイアウトシステム), and the
frame is one node in it: frames join to each other and to a family of other tables.
Two constants hold that family together, and Snow Peak publishes neither -- they are
read off the dimensions, the same way the 250mm unit pitch was:
400mm  the fire-side datum. EVERY table in the system stands 400mm tall, and the
IGT Low leg (CK-112) is 400mm. So 'the Connection Table is compatible with
IGT using Low Height Legs' is not a suggestion, it is arithmetic.
496mm  the shared depth. The IGT frame is 496 deep; the Takibi My Table is 496 deep;
the corner pieces are 496 square. They meet flush.
Every rule below quotes the vendor copy it came from. Where no rule could be sourced,

LV-381.name: Connection Table
LV-381.evidence: "compatible with most IGT Extensions using Low Height Legs, and can be connected with the Jikaro Firering Table to create an extended fire-safe table space."

ST-050.name: Jikaro Firering Table
ST-050.evidence: "compatible with the Iron Grill Table for additional extension possibilities." Built to ring a Takibi Fire & Grill -- the 600mm opening is the fire pit. It stands at 400mm, the system datum, so anything hooked to it takes the 400mm IGT Low leg -- and Snow Peak's own photo (JP a011) shows exactly that: a Bamboo IGT Table hooked to one outer edge, standing on 400mm legs, its near end carried by the Jikaro.
_it_is_four_pieces: FOUR identical trapezoid segments, and they go together either way round. That is not
a detail -- it is two different tables, and the planner needs both.
The two plan views (JP a007 = long edge inward, a008 = short edge inward) are shot at
DIFFERENT SCALES, by a factor of 1.26, so nothing can be read across them directly.
What crosses is the SEGMENT: it is the same physical piece in both, so its long side,
short side and height are the invariant, and they are what ties the photographs
together.
a007, long edge in  : outer 1069px, opening 565px, straight sides 347px
a008, short edge in : outer 1068px, opening 439px, straight sides 712px
the scale ratio, read off the segment three ways:
long sides   712/565 = 1.260
short sides  439/347 = 1.265
heights    314.5/252 = 1.248        agree to 1.4%
Calibrate on the published 1120x1120 / opening 600 -- which is the a007 config, because
its ratio 0.53 matches and a008's 0.41 does not -- and everything falls out, and CHECKS:
segment: long 600, short 365, height 260mm
(slant ~24 deg. The outer chamfer comes out at 45 deg for free, whatever the sides
are -- it runs from one segment's outer corner to the next one's, and symmetry
does the rest.)
the SHORT side is measured TWICE, independently: 364mm as a007's outer straight edge,
366mm as a008's opening. And a008's bbox comes out 885 predicted vs 890 measured.
Two photographs at two scales agree with each other and with the spec table, once the
scales are kept apart. That is the check that says the model is right.

long_in.name: long edge in (spread)
long_in.note: The published configuration -- the spread/'long edge in' assembly the user calls WAI-BEN (outward). A 600mm fire opening (= a 2-Unit IGT bay when bridged), and four short 365mm outer edges to hook onto.

short_in.name: short edge in (compact)
short_in.note: Compact -- the 'short edge in' assembly the user calls NEI-BEN (inward), Snow Peak's 'square mode'. A 365mm opening (= a 1-Unit IGT bay when bridged) and four long 600mm outer edges. The same four pieces, turned around.

ST-050.bridge_note: The central opening only becomes usable IGT space with an OPTIONAL bridge accessory laid across it (2 brackets over the opening + N bars sliding into their grooves, stainless). Like the connection hook and rail joint, a bridge cannot stand alone -- it modifies the Jikaro. See layout.bridges. Opening 600 -> 2-Unit bridge, opening 365 -> 1-Unit bridge; the opening size is what decides which fits.
ST-050.hook_edges: The four OUTER STRAIGHT sides. Snow Peak's photo (a011) shows a Bamboo IGT Table hooked to one of them, on 400mm legs. The four 45-degree CHAMFERS are not offered: nothing says a board hooks there, and the planner does not guess.

GF-051.name: Takibi Garden Table
GF-051.excluded_reason: Fixed garden furniture -- assembled in place, not carried or moved. Out of scope for a planner of a PORTABLE kit, even though its connection to IGT is real. Kept here, flagged, rather than deleted. See overrides.json.
GF-051.evidence: "Use the Takibi Garden Table with the Takibi Fire & Grill and Bamboo Extensions" -- the Bamboo Extensions are IGT parts (CK-118TR etc).

GF-052.name: Takibi Garden Table XL
GF-052.excluded_reason: Fixed garden furniture like GF-051, and larger. Out of scope for a portable-kit planner; kept and flagged.

LV-039.name: Takibi My Table
LV-039.evidence: Not stated in the copy, but it is 496mm wide -- exactly the IGT frame depth -- and 400mm tall, the system datum. It is built to butt against a frame's short side.

LV-310.name: Stainless Kitchen Table
LV-310.evidence: "tabletop that seamlessly integrates with the Iron Grill Table"; LV-312: "attaches to the Stainless Steel Kitchen Table to allow the insertion of an IGT Four Unit Frame within the length of the table. Set includes two Connectors." Note the 1100mm height -- this one does NOT sit at the datum.

expandables._comment: Self-contained tables whose FORM changes: a discrete config alters both footprint AND how many IGT unit-slots the part exposes. Passed through untouched by build_catalog (it only processes tables/joints/corners/ecosystems), so CK-090 keeps its standalone role. bay_* describes the IGT slot region a config exposes, in the node's local frame.

CK-090.name: Extension IGT
CK-090.note: Two laminated-bamboo tabletops on one aluminium stand that slide apart. Closed it is a plain ~3-unit-long table; slid fully open it exposes a central 2-Unit IGT bay (500x360) between the two tops. Catalogue title carries a 'Risk of tipping over' warning -- the open span is cantilevered.

expanded.name: expanded (open)
expanded.note: Fully slid open. 1348x498 overall (~5 units end to end); the 508mm the tops travel opens exactly a 2-Unit (500mm) IGT bay in the middle. From the manual set-contents line (2ユニット=W)500x360.

collapsed.name: collapsed (closed)
collapsed.note: Tops pushed together. 840x498 (~3 units); a plain table, no IGT bay exposed. Manual 〈最小〉840x498.

bridges._comment: OPTIONAL bridge accessories for the Jikaro (ST-050). Each lays across the central fire opening and turns it into IGT unit-slots. They cannot exist on their own -- like the connection hook (CK-175) and rail joint (XCK-128), a bridge only modifies the Jikaro -- so the planner never places one as its own node; it is a toggle on a Jikaro and its SKU shows up in that Jikaro's parts list. Real Snow Peak accessories, mostly limited / after-market now.

ST-051.name: Jikaro Table 1 Unit Bridge
ST-051.availability: Official Snow Peak SKU (sits next to ST-050). Now rare / discontinued; secondary market.
ST-051.note: Bridges the 365mm opening of the compact (short-edge-in) Jikaro to give one IGT unit. Recommended for the 'square mode' the copy mentions.

CPL-JT2U.name: Jikaro Top 2 Unit Bridge
CPL-JT2U.contents: 2 main brackets + 2 bridge bars + storage pouch
CPL-JT2U.availability: Official version is the SEPPOUSAI (Snow Peak Festival) 2023 Autumn limited edition; CPL-JT2U is the after-market equivalent (BIGTENT). Provides space for 1 or 2 IGT-unit appliances.
CPL-JT2U.note: Two brackets rest over the 600mm opening of the spread (long-edge-in) Jikaro; the two bars slide into grooves on the brackets to make a 2-Unit IGT bay.

self_igt._comment: Self-contained IGTs that ARE 3-unit frames in a fixed body: they ship with custom bamboo/teak tops that have NO separate SKU, and those tops LIFT OUT so standard IGT units drop into the frame -- which is what makes them IGTs. Modelled as a 3-unit bay whose default fill is the wood top; a module simply takes a top piece's place. Passed through untouched by build_catalog. units in half-unit tiles = units*2.

CK-080R.note: Entry IGT. Tops = 2x one-unit + 2x half-unit bamboo (manual set-contents); 833x440 body, ~41mm end margins round the 750mm 3-unit run.

CK-080R-EC.note: Entry IGT, black finish -- same 3-unit frame as CK-080R.

CK-180.note: IGT Slim. SIX removable half-unit teak panels = a 3-unit frame; any panel lifts out for a stovetop or workspace. 940x403 body.

tta.name: Table Top Architect
tta.note: A SEPARATE system, not an IGT accessory. TTA clamps to the edge of ANY tabletop — an IGT frame, a bamboo extension, a Takibi table, someone else's table — and hangs its own fittings off it. It coexists with IGT constantly, which is why it is easy to mistake for part of it, but nothing in it depends on the IGT grid: a TTA clamp consumes no unit and cares only that there is an edge to grip.

CK-151.name: IGT Height Adjuster
CK-151.note: Joins two tables at DIFFERENT heights. It is not a leg modifier -- the English name misleads; the Japanese one (段差 = level difference) says exactly what it does. A 320mm post, 25.4mm across, the same diameter as a leg, sold in pairs.
CK-151.evidence: "allow for integration of different table heights. Set your cooking space to a standing height, then dining while seated. To use, slide into the edge of the IGT Frame, then attach the next table at preferred height and tighten the knobs."

CK-175.name: IGT Connection Hook
CK-175.note: JP-only. 45g each. Joins frames at the same height.
CK-175.evidence: JP catalog: IGTコネクションフック.

LV-312.name: Stainless Kitchen Table IGT Frame Connector
LV-312.note: Drops a 4-unit frame INTO the length of the Stainless Kitchen Table. Ships as a pair.
LV-312.evidence: "Attach the Connectors to either side of the Stainless Steel Kitchen Table, add the IGT Four Unit Frame, and continue building out a custom IGT setup. Set includes two Connectors."

CK-118TR.evidence: "Use it to extend the table 90 degrees to the left and create a wraparound cooking and dining space." JP name: マルチファンクションテーブルコーナーL竹.
